title: Stable de novo protein design via joint conformational landscape and sequence optimization
core_idea: Jointly optimize models that predict sequence from structure (p(sequence|structure)) and structure from sequence (p(structure|sequence)) so the design process explores and refines the full conformational landscape—adjusting both sequence and backbone—to favor the target fold as the lowest-energy conformation and reduce alternative misfolded states. The study implements a four-model protocol (including trros, trmrf, proteinMPNN, and a joint trros+trmrf model), systematically compares objectives, and pairs computational design with large-scale experimental folding-stability measurements.
tldr: The paper proposes and systematically evaluates jointly optimizing sequence-to-structure and structure-to-sequence models to better model conformational landscapes and design de novo proteins whose target conformation is prioritized, with computational protocols tested alongside high-throughput stability assays.
